# UnknownPolicy

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs generate` from `schemas/policy/v1.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The unknown-application policy (#39). Every field is optional in a
document; the defaults block every unknown object.

Appears at: `/policy/unknown`.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_request` | boolean | no | `false` |  | 1.0.0 | When an unknown object is blocked, the user may ask for approval (#11). |
| `by_location` | map of [`Level`](types.md#level) | no |  | keys: one of `user_profile`, `temp`, `user_writable_other`, `program_files`, `windows`, `other_fixed`, `removable`, `network`, `optical`, `ads` | 1.0.0 | The level per location class. |
| `by_origin` | map of [`Level`](types.md#level) | no |  | keys: one of `internet`, `email_attachment`, `removable_copy`, `network_share`, `trusted_source`, `preexisting`, `unknown` | 1.0.0 | The level per origin. |
| `by_type` | object | no |  | keys: one of `executable`, `library`, `driver`, `script.powershell`, `script.batch`, `script.cmd`, `script.vbscript`, `script.jscript`, `script.wsf`, `script.wsc`, `script.python`, `script.java`, `script.reg`, `script.other`, `installer`, `compiled_html`, `html_application`, `control_panel_applet`, `packaged_app`, `command`, `com_object` | 1.0.0 | The level per object type. `restrict` only for executables, scripts and installers; `prompt` not for libraries or drivers. |
| `default` | [`Level`](types.md#level) | no | `"block"` |  | 1.0.0 | The level when no entry below applies. The default is `block`. |

| `preexisting_policy` | [`PreexistingPolicy`](types.md#preexistingpolicy) | no | `"baseline_only"` |  | 1.0.0 | What happens to files present at install. |
| `preset` | [`CompliancePreset`](types.md#compliancepreset) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The compliance preset this policy started from, if any. |
| `prompt` | [`PromptSettings`](prompt-settings.md) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | How the `prompt` level asks. |
| `restrict_profile` | [`ContainmentProfileRef`](types.md#containmentprofileref) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The containment profile of the `restrict` level (#14). Required when any level, or the prompt's fallback, is `restrict`. |
| `scope_groups` | array of [`ScopeGroup`](scope-group.md) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The effective form of where these settings apply, written by the hierarchy (#37): a subject in **every** scope of at least one group. Empty, the default, means no further limit. An effective policy has no `policy.scope`, so each contributing policy's `scope` and `scopes` become groups here: `scope` and each of `scopes`, one group per entry (`UnknownPolicy::scope_groups_of`). The settings then apply exactly where they applied in each contributing policy, never more widely. At most 1000 groups of at most 8 scopes (the hierarchy writes groups of 1 or 2). A policy document may carry it, so that an effective policy validates as any document, but is meant to write `scope` and `scopes` instead. |
| `scopes` | array of [`Scope`](scope.md) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | Where these settings apply, besides the policy's `scope` (#38): a subject in at least one of these scopes, at most 1000. Empty, the default, means wherever the policy applies. A subject outside it is decided by the built-in implicit deny (`crate::unknown`). |

Unknown fields are rejected.
